notable_anecdotes: Corruption joke for the post-election context: 'What is the difference between an ordinary robber and a corrupt politician? The ordinary robber chooses the people he or she will rob. On the other hand, the politician is chosen by the people whom he or she will rob.'
CJP's comment to Katrina Gaw on her 5th place: 'I told her she was better than I because I ranked only No. 6, so she must excel my being only chief justice!'

The library anecdote: CJP tried to convince eldest grandson Miguel to take up law by showing him his library and promising to bequeath it. 'Ironically, it turned him off. He rushed to his grandmother Leni, saying that he would not take up law because he could not imagine himself reading all the voluminous books in my library.' Instead, Miguel took BS Industrial Engineering at UP and MBA at Babson College (Boston, #1 in entrepreneurship in the US, ahead of Harvard, Stanford and MIT).

Justice Carpio and Bernabe's SC inner sanctum interview rooms: 'These rooms constitute the sacred inner sanctum of the temple of justice in our country where, normally, only justices are allowed entry when Division cases are deliberated upon and decided. No secretaries, clerks or aides dare enter these rooms when the justices perform their rituals and duties. This is indeed a great privilege for our scholars and winners, who even before passing the bar examinations were already allowed entry to the Supreme Court's inner sanctum.'

Ayala Chairman Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala's instant commitment: 'When I advised [him] of this unique contest... he immediately agreed to fund the project, as an extra addition to Ayala's normal budget for philanthropy.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered May 18, 2019 at the FLP 2019 Awards Ceremony at Ateneo de Manila Professional Schools -- the first ceremony featuring bar exam topnotchers -- this three-part closing address by CJP opens with a post-mid-term election joke ('the ordinary robber chooses who to rob; the politician is chosen by the people whom he will rob') and two senior self-deprecation jokes. The Congratulations section celebrates FLP scholar Sean James Borja (Ateneo valedictorian and bar exam numero uno -- total P625,000 in scholarship and awards over two years), Katrina Gaw (5th place -- total P300,000; absent on a celebratory trip; CJP notes: 'I ranked only No. 6, so she must excel my being only chief justice!'), 20 new scholars (P200,000 each), and dissertation writing winners: 3rd prizes (additional P100,000 each), Diana Lou Boado of Lyceum of PH (2nd, P200,000), and Josiah David Quising of FEU (1st, P300,000 -- also a former FLP scholar). Parents are asked to stand; CJP envies them, confessing that none of his five children took up law, and that even his eldest grandson Miguel -- shown the family library as an inducement -- was turned off and instead went to Babson College for an MBA (#1 in entrepreneurship, ahead of Harvard, Stanford and MIT). The Appreciation section thanks Justices Carpio and Bernabe (both abroad -- SC at recess), who held final interviews in the SC's Division Conference Rooms ('the sacred inner sanctum... where normally only justices are allowed entry when Division cases are deliberated') -- a privilege for scholars 'who even before passing the bar examinations were already allowed entry.' Tan Yan Kee Foundation, Ayala Corporation (Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala 'immediately agreed' to fund the Dissertation Contest), Ateneo (venue and new professorial chair Dean Hofilena), and Inquirer (Sandy Prieto-Romualdez's full-color back-page ad) are all thanked. The Explanation section articulates FLP's merit-first-need-as-tiebreaker selection principle and announces the formation of the FLP Scholars Society.
